f.title: Treat all spontaneous reports as suspected adverse reactions unless the reporter excludes causality
f.statement: For regulatory reporting purposes, all spontaneous reports notified by healthcare professionals or consumers are considered suspected adverse reactions, even where the causal relationship is unknown or unstated, because they convey the suspicion of the primary source, unless the reporter specifically states that the events are unrelated or that a causal relationship can be excluded.
f.applicability: Medicinal products for human use authorised in Nigeria (GVP Chapter 5, PV-GDL-005-02)

rows.quote: For regulatory reporting purposes, as detailed in ICH-E2D, if an event is spontaneously reported, even if the relationship is unknown or unstated, it meets the definition of an adverse reaction. Therefore, all spontaneous reports notified by healthcare professionals or consumers are considered suspected adverse reactions, since they convey the suspicions of the primary sources, unless the reporters specifically state that they believe the events to be unrelated or that a causal relationship can be excluded.

f.title: Treat consumer reports confirmed by an HCP as medically confirmed and update the ICSR
f.statement: Where suspected adverse reactions initially reported by a consumer are subsequently confirmed by a healthcare professional, the ICSR should be considered medically confirmed and updated at case level (E2B(R2)) or reaction level (E2B(R3)).

f.title: Classify seriousness using the ICH-E2A criteria
f.statement: A serious adverse reaction is any untoward medical occurrence that at any dose results in death; is life-threatening (patient at risk of death at the time of the event, not hypothetically); requires inpatient hospitalisation or prolongs existing hospitalisation; results in persistent or significant disability/incapacity; is a congenital anomaly/birth defect; or is an important medical event.
f.applicability: Medicinal products for human use authorised in Nigeria (GVP Chapter 5, PV-GDL-005-02)

rows.quote: As described in ICH-E2A, a serious adverse reaction corresponds to any untoward medical occurrence that at any dose:  results in death;  is life-threatening (NOTE: The term “life-threatening” in the definition of “serious” refers to an AE/ADR in which the patient was at risk of death at the time of the AE/ADR; it does not refer to an AE/ADR that hypothetically might have caused death if it were more severe);  requires inpatient hospitalisation or results in prolongation of existing hospitalisation;  results in persistent or significant disability/incapacity;  is a congenital anomaly/birth defect;  is an important medical event as described below

Where one or more serious suspected adverse reactions are reported in an ICSR, seriousness should be documented at case level (ICH-E2B(R2)) or for each suspected adverse reaction (ICH-E2B(R3)), depending on the E2B format used.
f.applicability: Medicinal products for human use authorised in Nigeria (GVP Chapter 5, PV-GDL-005-02)

f.title: Assess expectedness against local labelling; treat uncertain cases as unexpected
f.statement: An AE/ADR shall be considered unexpected if it is not listed in the current regional or local product labelling; if its nature, severity, specificity or clinical outcome is not consistent with the labelling; or if it is reported with a fatal outcome, unless the labelling explicitly states that the reaction may be associated with a fatal outcome. Where it is uncertain whether an AE/ADR is expected or unexpected, it shall be treated as unexpected for regulatory reporting purposes.

Where there is uncertainty as to whether an AE/ADR should be classified as expected or unexpected it shall be treated as unexpected for regulatory reporting purposes.

f.title: Collect and collate all suspected ADR reports from unsolicited and solicited sources
f.statement: The MAH should take appropriate measures to collect and collate all reports of suspected adverse reactions from unsolicited or solicited sources; the PV system should help ensure reports are authentic, legible, accurate, consistent, verifiable and as complete as possible. The system should collect and record all reports from HCPs, consumers or post-authorisation studies, and MAHs should not refuse to consider reports from patients and HCPs.

rows.quote: Reports associated with suspected adverse reactions should be routinely followed-up to ensure that the information is as complete as possible with regards to the symptoms,
rows.review_note: Review: new row split from 0039 (5.5.3.3); quote stops at 'symptoms,' because of a page header; the rest of the list is the continuation. f.title: Report lack of therapeutic efficacy within 15 calendar days
f.statement: Reports of lack of therapeutic efficacy should be reported within 15 calendar days and followed up if incomplete, unless the reporter has specifically stated that the outcome was due to disease progression and not related to the medicinal product.
f.applicability: Medicinal products for human use authorised in Nigeria (GVP Chapter 5, PV-GDL-005-02)
f.exceptions: Not where the reporter states the outcome was due to disease progression and unrelated

rows.deadline: Within 15 calendar days
rows.quote: Reports of lack of therapeutic efficacy should be reported within 15 calendar days and followed-up if incomplete unless the reporter has specifically stated that the outcome was due to disease progression and was not related to the medicinal product.
rows.review_note: Review: statement narrowed to 5.5.4.1 (the quote); 5.5.4.2 clinical judgement and 5.5.4.3 vaccines moved to new rows 0083 and 0084. Level kept Recommended ('should'); this 15-day timeline is specific to lack of efficacy and is not stated as mandatory elsewhere. Double-check: confirmed: 'should be reported within 15 calendar days' with the disease-progression exception; below 90: passive, actor inferred.

f.title: Use clinical judgement for lack-of-efficacy reports; report new resistance within 15 days
f.statement: Clinical judgement should be used when reporting lack of efficacy: e.g. an antibiotic used in a life-threatening situation where it was not appropriate for the infective agent should not be reported, but a life-threatening infection where lack of efficacy appears due to a newly resistant strain of a previously susceptible bacterium should be reported within 15 days.
f.applicability: Medicinal products for human use authorised in Nigeria (GVP Chapter 5, PV-GDL-005-02)

rows.deadline: Within 15 days (newly resistant strain cases)
rows.quote: Clinical judgment should be used when reporting cases of lack of therapeutic efficacy. For example, an antibiotic used in a life-threatening situation where the medicinal product was not in fact appropriate for the infective agent should not be reported. However, a life-threatening infection, where the lack of therapeutic efficacy appears to be due to the development of a newly resistant strain of a bacterium previously regarded as susceptible, should be reported within 15 days.
rows.review_note: Review: new row split from 0040 (5.5.4.2). Double-check: confirmed; below 90: passive wording; the MAH actor is inferred, not named in the quote; example-based.

deadline_rule.clock_start: information containing the minimum reporting criteria has been brought to the attention of the Marketing Authorisation Holder
deadline_rule.applies_to: Lack of efficacy in a life-threatening infection apparently due to a newly resistant bacterial strain

f.title: Report vaccine lack of immunogenic effect
f.statement: For vaccines, cases of lack of immunogenic effect should be reported, in particular to highlight potential signals of reduced immunogenicity in a subgroup, waning immunity or strain replacement; spontaneously reported HCP cases may signal strain replacement needing prompt action and possibly PASS. CIOMS/WHO vaccine pharmacovigilance guidance on vaccine failure may be followed.
f.applicability: Medicinal products for human use authorised in Nigeria (GVP Chapter 5, PV-GDL-005-02)

rows.quote: For vaccines, cases of lack of immunogenic effect should be reported, in particular with the view to highlight potential signals of reduced immunogenicity in a sub-group of vaccinees, waning immunity, or strain replacement. With regard to the latter, it is considered that spontaneously reported cases of lack of immunogenic effect by a healthcare professional may constitute a signal of strain replacement. Such a signal may need prompt action and further investigation through post-authorisation safety studies as appropriate. General guidance regarding the monitoring of vaccines failure, provided in the Report of CIOMS/WHO Working Group on Vaccine Pharmacovigilance, may be followed.
rows.review_note: Review: new row split from 0040 (5.5.4.3). Double-check: confirmed; below 90: passive wording; the MAH actor is inferred, not named in the quote; signal/CIOMS sentences are descriptive or 'may'.

f.title: Report ADRs with substandard/falsified products and notify confirmed defects
f.statement: A valid ICSR should be reported for ADRs associated with suspected or confirmed substandard/falsified products; MAHs should have a system to investigate promptly and notify confirmed quality defects to the manufacturer and the Agency.
f.applicability: Medicinal products for human use authorised in Nigeria (GVP Chapter 5, PV-GDL-005-02)

rows.quote: When a report of suspected adverse reactions is associated with a suspected or confirmed substandard and falsified medicinal product, a valid ICSR should be reported. The seriousness of the ICSR is linked to the seriousness of the reported suspected adverse reactions in accordance with the definitions provided in section 5.3 Definitions. 5.5.5.2 In addition, to protect public health, it may become necessary to implement urgent measures such as the recall of one or more defective batch(es) of a medicinal product from the market. Therefore, Marketing Authorisation Holders should have a system in place to ensure that reports of suspected adverse reactions related to substandard and falsified medicinal products are investigated promptly and that confirmed quality defects of substandard and falsified products are notified to manufacturer and to the Agency.
rows.review_note: Review: quote extended to cover 5.5.5.1 (valid ICSR for substandard/falsified products) and 5.5.5.2. Double-check: confirmed; below 90: first sentence passive (MAH named only in the second).

f.title: Report suspected transmission of infectious agents as serious within 15 days
f.statement: Any suspected transmission of an infectious agent via a medicinal product should be considered a serious adverse reaction and reported within 15 days per 5.4.6; if no other criterion applies, seriousness should be recorded as an important medical event. This also applies to vaccines. (The underlying duty to report serious suspected adverse reactions within 15 calendar days is mandatory under 5.4.6.1.1; see 0024.)
f.applicability: Medicinal products for human use authorised in Nigeria (GVP Chapter 5, PV-GDL-005-02)

rows.deadline: Within 15 days
rows.quote: For the purposes of reporting, any suspected transmission of an infectious agent via a medicinal product should be considered as a serious adverse reaction and such cases should be reported within 15 days in accordance with requirements outlined in section 5.4.6 Reporting Timelines. If no other criterion is applicable, the seriousness of this ICSR should be considered as important medicinal event. This also applies to vaccines.
rows.review_note: Review: quote extended to the whole of 5.5.6.1; 5.5.6.2 (blood/plasma products) moved to new row 0085. f.title: Communicate suspected infectious transmission from blood/plasma products
f.statement: For medicinal products derived from human blood or plasma (where haemovigilance procedures may also apply), the MAH should have a system to communicate suspected transmission of an infectious agent to the manufacturer, the relevant blood establishment(s) and the Agency.
f.applicability: Medicinal products for human use authorised in Nigeria (GVP Chapter 5, PV-GDL-005-02)

rows.quote: In the case of medicinal products derived from human blood or human plasma, haemovigilance procedures may also apply. Therefore the Marketing Authorisation Holder should have a system in place to communicate suspected transmission via a medicinal product of an infectious agent to the manufacturer, the relevant blood establishment(s) and the Agency.

f.title: Consider known and unknown agents when assessing suspected infectious transmission
f.statement: Transmission of an infectious agent may be suspected from clinical signs, symptoms or laboratory findings of infection in an exposed patient; emphasis should be on agents known to be transmissible via medicinal products, but unknown agents should always be considered.
f.applicability: Medicinal products for human use authorised in Nigeria (GVP Chapter 5, PV-GDL-005-02)

rows.quote: A transmission of an infectious agent may be suspected from clinical signs or symptoms, or laboratory findings indicating an infection in a patient exposed to a medicinal product. Emphasis should be on the detection of infections/infectious agents known to be potentially transmitted via a medicinal product, but the occurrence of unknown agents should also always be considered.
rows.review_note: Review: new row: 5.5.6.3 not captured. 5.5.6.4 (discriminate cause vs source) is not given a row because its quote would cross a line-end hyphen ('immuno-' / 'suppressed'). Double-check: confirmed; below 90: first sentence descriptive and the 'should' is passive; actor inferred.

f.title: Apply quality-defect procedures where contamination is confirmed
f.statement: Confirmed contamination of the medicinal product (including inadequate inactivation/attenuation of infectious agents used as active substances) strengthens the evidence for transmission and may suggest a quality defect, for which the 5.5.5 procedures for quality defects and substandard/falsified products should be applied.
f.applicability: Medicinal products for human use authorised in Nigeria (GVP Chapter 5, PV-GDL-005-02)

rows.quote: Confirmation of contamination (including inadequate inactivation/attenuation of infectious agents as active substances) of the concerned medicinal product increases the evidence for transmission of an infectious agent and may therefore be suggestive of a quality defect for which the procedures detailed in 5.5.5 Suspected adverse reactions related to quality defect or Substandard and falsified medicinal products should be applied.
rows.review_note: Review: new row: 5.5.6.5 not captured. Double-check: confirmed; below 90: passive wording; the MAH actor is inferred, not named in the quote.

f.title: Notify emerging safety issues per GVP Module IX
f.statement: Emerging safety issues should be notified to the Agency per GVP Module IX Signal Detection, in addition to ICSR submission where they concern a single case.
f.applicability: Medicinal products for human use authorised in Nigeria (GVP Chapter 5, PV-GDL-005-02)

rows.quote: Events/observations may occur in relation to an authorised medicinal product, which may have major impacts on the risk-benefit balance of the product and/or on patients or public health. They may require urgent attention of the agency and could warrant prompt regulatory action and communication to patients and healthcare professionals. These important new evidences should be considered as emerging safety issues. They should be notified to the Agency in accordance with the requirements provided in GVP Module IX Signal Detection. This is in addition to the ICSR submission requirements detailed in section 5.4.5 Reporting of ICSR when the emerging safety issue refers to a single case of suspected adverse reactions.
rows.review_note: Review: quote extended to the whole of 5.5.7.1 so it proves the 'in addition to ICSR submission' part. Double-check: confirmed; below 90: 'They should be notified' passive; actor inferred.

f.title: Apply the same reporting to donated products; MAH or receiving entity responsible
f.statement: Suspected adverse reactions associated with medicinal products supplied through donation programmes (e.g., by governments, international organisations or NGOs) shall be subject to the same reporting requirements and timelines as authorised products in Nigeria. Where an MAH exists for the donated product in Nigeria, it shall be responsible for the collection, assessment and reporting of all valid ICSRs per this Chapter.
f.applicability: Medicinal products for human use authorised in Nigeria (GVP Chapter 5, PV-GDL-005-02)

f.title: Receiving entity reports ADRs for donated products when there is no MAH
f.statement: Where there is no identifiable MAH in Nigeria, the entity or person authorised to receive the donated product (e.g., government agency, public health programme, implementing partner) shall be responsible for collecting, assessing and reporting suspected adverse reactions, and shall ensure valid ICSRs are submitted within the timelines, mechanisms exist for collection, documentation, follow-up and transmission, and safety information from HCPs, patients or donors is promptly evaluated and reported.
f.applicability: Medicinal products for human use authorised in Nigeria (GVP Chapter 5, PV-GDL-005-02)

rows.actor: Entity or person authorised to receive the donated product (no MAH in Nigeria)
rows.quote: In situations where there is no identifiable MAH in Nigeria, the overall responsibility for the collection, assessment and reporting of suspected adverse reactions to the Agency shall rest with the entity or person authorised to receive the donated product in Nigeria (e.g. government agency, public health programme, or designated implementing partner). 5.5.8.4 Such entity or person shall ensure that:  all reports meeting the minimum criteria for a valid ICSR are submitted in accordance with the timelines specified in this Chapter;  appropriate mechanisms are in place for the collection, documentation, follow-up and transmission of adverse reaction reports; and  relevant safety information received from healthcare professionals, patients, or donor organisations is promptly evaluated and reported as required.

f.title: Promptly review donor safety information and submit as ICSRs or significant safety information
f.statement: Safety information on donated products received from international partners or donor organisations shall be promptly reviewed and, where applicable, submitted to the Agency as ICSRs or as significant safety information.

f.title: Submit benefit-risk-impacting information immediately during application review
f.statement: Between application submission and authorisation, the applicant must ensure information that could impact the benefit-risk balance is immediately submitted to the Agency.

It is the responsibility of the applicant to ensure that this information is immediately submitted to the Agency.

f.title: Continue collecting ADR reports after suspension of the marketing authorisation
